author: sonnet
label: c2-nat-sonnet-01
changes: Added the level-to-role mapping (1 primary, 2 secondary, 3 manager) to the escalation_step row, because Q4 asked which person each level pages.

Extended the notification row with level, state values and lease_until, and added a 'How pages and notices are sent' section with the 60-second lease and send loop, because Q5 and Q8 showed retries and lease were unexplained.
Said that each evaluator has its own timer and derives the tick from the clock, and that unhandled ticks are backfilled, because Q1 asked what the scheduler is.
Stated that consecutive breaches are read from the last 3 evaluation rows, breach_count is audit only and a missing tick breaks the run, because Q2 found this unclear.
Fixed the diagram's 'reset breach streak' wording and added a missing 'breaching, fewer than 3, no incident' condition, because the old branch was wrong.
Made the escalation steps conditional on the incident insert creating a row, in the notes and the diagram, because Q3 found the ON CONFLICT case undefined.
Added a 'What an acknowledgement does' section covering what an ack stops, what it leaves open and how the webhook finds the incident and verifies the signature, for Q6 and Q7.
Made resolved notices copy the page's level so the unique key holds, and said the send loop sends them, for Q8.
Updated the failure table rows for worker crash, both channels failing and missed ticks to match.
Added an Open questions section for the provider echo and signing assumption and for the lease and polling values.
Escalation due times in the diagram changed from T to opened_at, and opened_at defined as the incident insert time, so backfilled ticks cannot fire all levels at once (Q9).
Retry cap defined (5 attempts) with a failure-table row saying what happens at the cap, plus an open question about nobody being reachable (Q10).
Added a rule that a missing tick resets healthy_streak, and clarified long metrics outage behaviour in the failure table and diagram (Q11).
Added the ack_log table and used it in the diagram and failure table for late or repeated acks (Q12).
Added the oncall_cache table and defined the no-cache fallback (step stays pending, retried each poll) in the failure table and diagram (Q13).
Added a diagram branch and a text sentence for a non-breaching evaluation with no open incident: only the evaluation row is stored (Q14).
Added a two-sentence-plus summary at the top that states today's cron-and-inbox setup, the main flow and why it is shaped this way. It replaces the old opening paragraph.

Added a Terms section defining tick, evaluation, breaching, healthy, incident, escalation step, notification and idempotency key, paging provider, on-call schedule service, partial unique index and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, because the questions showed newcomers got stuck on these names.
Moved the sequence diagram to just after the summary and terms, with all notes after it, as the skill requires for diagrams.

Restructured the notes into where state lives, evaluator coordination, timers, sending, ack, silent-brief rules, failures and open questions, and merged the repeated statements of the same rule (incident insert guard, tick-row-breaks-run, ack-does-not-resolve, due times anchored to opened_at) into one place each.
Merged the 'healthy' definition and the 'rate between 1% and 2%' rule so each is stated once. The healthy definition moved into Terms and the neither-state rule stayed under silent-brief rules.
Cut the repeated explanation of ack_log in the failure table and the ack section, and trimmed the failure-table wording that restated the diagram.

Dropped nothing from the first version: all tables, the 2%/500/3-in-a-row/1%/10-minute rules, escalation times, push-then-SMS, resolved notices, the two-instance design, the 5s polling, the 15-minute backfill and the tolerated ack race are still present.

Added the `ack_log`, `oncall_cache` and `level` and `lease_until` fields, and the 5-attempt cap, as in the revised version, and kept the answers to the junior's questions at the step where each applies.
